name: CrUX
what_it_holds: Official Google Chrome team repo for the Chrome UX Report: example BigQuery SQL queries, dataset schema docs, changelog of CrUX releases, issue tracker for the public BigQuery dataset `chrome-ux-report`. No committed rows itself; it is the canonical pointer/method for querying per-origin popularity rank and Core Web Vitals monthly since ~2018 via BigQuery (free tier covers occasional queries).
why_useful: Authoritative source and ready-made SQL for pulling airbnb.com's monthly popularity-rank decile/percentile history from 2018 onward if crux-dumps' 2021+ coverage isn't long enough or a fresher pull is needed.
size_hint: code + docs only; underlying BigQuery dataset is multi-TB
themes: Web-traffic estimates and domain ranks: Similarweb scrapers or samples, Cloudflare Radar API, Chrome UX Report popularity rank, Tranco, Majestic Million, Common Crawl host-graph rank
Search/SEO and referral data: Bing/Google keyword volume tools, SERP scrapers, Common Crawl web graph, backlink datasets, AI-bot crawler traffic stats (Cloudflare, Vercel)
Retail and ecommerce alt-data open samples (web-scraped prices, Amazon rank), as templates for platform KPI nowcasting
why_all: Authoritative source and ready-made SQL for pulling airbnb.com's monthly popularity-rank decile/percentile history from 2018 onward if crux-dumps' 2021+ coverage isn't long enough or a fresher pull is needed.

CrUX's public BigQuery dataset covers per-origin real-Chrome-user metrics for airbnb.com and competitor domains monthly since 2017; this repo is just the query cookbook needed to pull it (gap 5 popularity-rank angle), not itself a data cache.

Matches gap #5 ("Chrome UX Report popularity rank") exactly; CrUX's origin popularity ranking (rank buckets by real Chrome traffic) is a free, monthly, historically-versioned alternative/complement to Similarweb-style traffic estimates for airbnb.com and competitor domains.

name: tranco-list
what_it_holds: Source code (Python: combined_lists.py, generate_daily_list.py, job_handler.py/job_server.py, generate_domain_parts.py) that produces the daily Tranco top-1M website ranking, a research-oriented, manipulation-hardened alternative to Alexa/Similarweb rankings; the live ranking lists themselves are served from tranco-list.eu (daily-updated, historical lists downloadable by date from that companion site), with the generation code open on GitHub.
why_useful: Tranco is explicitly designed to be a stable, citable, point-in-time domain-popularity ranking (each list has a fixed hash/date), which is exactly the point-in-time property the team's rules require and Google Trends lacked; could track airbnb.com vs vrbo.com/booking.com/expedia.com rank drift back to 2018.
size_hint: code only; external lists are ~1M domains/day since 2018

Retail and ecommerce alt-data open samples (web-scraped prices, Amazon rank), as templates for platform KPI nowcasting

name: crux-top-lists
what_it_holds: Monthly CSV.gz snapshots (columns: origin, rank) of Chrome's top ~1M sites derived from Google's public CrUX BigQuery dataset. Rank is bucketed (1000/10K/100K/1M) by pageload volume, both global and country-specific lists, cached under data/global/ back to roughly 2018 (monthly releases, second Tuesday of month). Current file at raw.githubusercontent.com/zakird/crux-top-lists/main/data/global/current.csv.gz. CITATION.cff present.
why_useful: airbnb.com's CrUX popularity-rank bucket over time is a free, long-running proxy for site-visit volume/engagement (gap #5, engagement/web-traffic). Monthly history since 2018 lets you build a point-in-time-ish visitation trend and compare against nights/GBV seasonality; also covers competitor domains (booking.com, vrbo.com, expedia.com) for relative-share reads.
size_hint: CSV.gz per month, ~1M rows each, chunked
license: Data under Google CrUX Dataset Terms; repo code likely permissive (check LICENSE file)

name: cc-webgraph
what_it_holds: Official Common Crawl Java toolkit to build host-level and domain-level web graphs from Common Crawl crawl data and compute PageRank / Harmonic Centrality rankings using the WebGraph framework. No graph files or ranking CSVs are committed in the repo itself — the actual host-rank datasets (domain harmonic-centrality and PageRank tables, updated with most Common Crawl monthly crawls) are announced/hosted separately on commoncrawl.org's webgraph release pages (e.g. s3://commoncrawl/projects/hyperlinkgraph/).
why_useful: This is the actual method behind 'Common Crawl host-graph rank' named in the theme brief — it lets you derive a host-level authority/rank score for airbnb.com and competitor domains from Common Crawl's periodically released host graphs (several per year, going back to ~2017), a free alternative to Tranco/Majestic that is already partially in scope given we hold a Common Crawl CDX index over airbnb.com (existing holding). Directly extends what we already hold rather than duplicating it.
time_coverage: per Common Crawl webgraph releases, ~2017-present, several/year
size_hint: toolkit only; source webgraphs are multi-GB, hosted externally at commoncrawl.org/web-graphs
duplicate_of_holding: extends existing Common Crawl CDX index over airbnb.com; different data product (host-graph rank vs CDX index)

Search/SEO and referral data: Bing/Google keyword volume tools, SERP scrapers, Common Crawl web graph, backlink datasets, AI-bot crawler traffic stats (Cloudflare, Vercel)
Common Crawl tooling: cdx-toolkit, warcio, host-level indexes, columnar index queries; datasets derived from Common Crawl for travel sites

Directly extends what we already hold rather than duplicating it.

This is the authoritative method for producing a Common Crawl-derived domain popularity/authority rank for airbnb.com and competitor domains over time (each crawl release gives a new rank snapshot, several times a year back to 2017) — a genuine point-in-time web-authority series, complementary to our existing Common Crawl CDX index over airbnb.com pages. Falls under gap 5 (web-traffic-like popularity proxies) as an acquisition method rather than a stored dataset; the actual rank tables must be pulled from Common Crawl's S3 announcements, which are public and free.

Could be re-run to derive a longitudinal 'web-graph rank' for airbnb.com vs vrbo.com/booking.com/expedia.com as an engagement/authority proxy (gap 5, 19). We already hold a CDX index over airbnb.com; this is the tool that turns crawl data into rank numbers.

A free, Common-Crawl-native alternative to Tranco/CrUX for a web-popularity time series on airbnb.com vs booking.com/expedia.com/vrbo.com -- directly targets gap 5 (web-traffic-estimate / rank proxies) and gap 19 (bot/crawler-visible presence) without any paid Similarweb-type feed. Ranks are released per crawl (roughly monthly/bi-monthly), so a multi-year vintage series is buildable by re-downloading historical rank releases.

name: python-mwviews
what_it_holds: Python client library (MIT, ~38 commits, 67 stars) for the Wikimedia pageviews API and static pageview dumps. Query per-article views, per-project views, and top-N articles by project/access-method/agent-type at daily/monthly granularity back to July 2015 (API) with dump-parsing support for older static counts. No data committed; pure acquisition tooling.
why_useful: Directly builds Gap 5 (Wikipedia pageviews tooling as an engagement/destination-demand proxy) — a maintained, well-documented one-command way to pull pageviews for any city/attraction/landmark Wikipedia article (e.g. 'New York City', 'Eiffel Tower', destination pages) as a free, high-frequency, near-real-time travel-interest signal comparable to Google Trends but with committable raw counts instead of blocked normalization.
time_coverage: API: July 2015-present daily; static dumps back further with separate parsing
last_activity: unspecified exact date; actively maintained per repo stats
themes: Wikipedia pageviews tooling and destination-demand datasets (pageviews for cities/attractions as tourism proxies)

One-command pull of Airbnb's (and Vrbo/Booking/Expedia/Vacasa's) Wikipedia pageview history as a free, long-run public-attention proxy (gap 5: engagement/web-traffic estimates) — Wikipedia pageviews are public back to ~2007-2015 depending on project, and this tool is simpler than hitting the raw REST API directly.

Same gap #5 use case as pageview-api but adds access to Wikimedia's static dump files, which is useful for getting a longer point-in-time-stamped Airbnb pageview history in one pull rather than many API calls.

Matches gap #5 ("Wikipedia pageviews tooling"); pageviews on the "Airbnb", "Vrbo", "Booking.com" etc. Wikipedia articles, or on destination-city pages, are a free, long-history, point-in-time-stable (dumps are dated) engagement/interest proxy that complements (and is less noisy for point-in-time purposes than) Google Trends, which the team already found not to work as pulled.

Lets the team pull daily pageviews for destination-city pages, 'Digital nomad', 'Short-term rental', 'FIFA World Cup 2026', or country-tourism pages as a free, easy, non-Airbnb travel-interest nowcast series -- a different construction from the Google Trends approach that already failed (0/162), and genuinely point-in-time since Wikipedia dump timestamps are fixed at publication.
